sources.title: From The Beast on the East River to Nathan AI 🚀
sources.text:
Think through a concern, speak about it, tell others, examine what the evidence shows, and act. This is a reading of the method Nathan Tabor describes from his KJV upbringing. The 2006 book and the 2025 posts document two applications of that approach. The links below open the relevant passages and examples.

The book excerpt is the published introduction. The Nathan AI records distinguish descriptions of the project, transcripts or claims shared by the author, and dated repository work. Dates from LinkedIn are computed from activity IDs and displayed in Eastern time. Each event supplies its source and evidence status.

sources.title: Nathan Tabor and Virginia Foxx on the NC-05 primary ballot
sources.text: The North Carolina statewide results list Nathan Tabor with 7,660 votes and Virginia Foxx with 13,119 votes in the same Republican primary for the Fifth Congressional District.

record.dateBasis: Election date

sources.title: UN oversight report on sexual exploitation and abuse in the Congo
sources.text: UN document A/59/661 records an investigation into allegations involving peacekeepers in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It provides an institutional source to read alongside the opening of the 2006 book.

record.dateBasis: Date printed on A/59/661

sources.title: The Beast on the East River — published introduction
sources.text: Nathan Tabor’s book examines the United Nations’ claims to authority and its record, with an emphasis on U.S. sovereignty, public scrutiny, and abuse by people entrusted with protecting vulnerable civilians. The linked source is “The Globe Is the Goal,” the 17-page introduction (printed pages vii–xxiii). The publication month comes from the edition listing linked below.

record.dateBasis: Publication month

sources.title: The Beast on the East River — edition listing
sources.text: The edition listing credits Nathan Tabor, gives the subtitle The U.N. Threat to America’s Sovereignty and Security, and lists October 2006.

record.dateBasis: Edition listing

sources.title: The Beast on the East River — protection and public scrutiny
sources.scope: Published primary excerpt, printed pages vii–ix
sources.text: The opening moves from a wartime scenario to reports of sexual exploitation and abuse involving United Nations peacekeepers in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Tabor challenges the gap between a protection mandate and the conduct reported under it, and argues for public scrutiny. Compare the linked UN oversight document for the scope of its own findings.

record.dateBasis: Publication month
record.evidence: Published primary excerpt, printed pages vii–ix

sources.title: The Beast on the East River — Solomon and Ecclesiastes
sources.scope: Published primary excerpt, printed page xviii
sources.text: The introduction attributes the observation about there being nothing new under the sun to Solomon, then applies it to recurring failures involving UN peacekeeping. Ecclesiastes 1:9 is a direct textual allusion in the published excerpt.

record.dateBasis: Publication month
record.evidence: Published primary excerpt, printed page xviii

sources.title: The Beast on the East River — call to immediate action
sources.scope: Published primary excerpt, printed page xxi
sources.text: Tabor connects his case for preserving personal liberty and national sovereignty with the lives of children and asks readers to engage with the evidence and respond.

original.text: This book is a call to immediate action

record.dateBasis: Publication month
record.evidence: Published primary excerpt, printed page xxi
